questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Net flux from a charge inside a closed surface
questions.learningObjective: compute electric flux from an enclosed charge
questions.stem: Interpreting a graph, a closed surface encloses a single charge of 3.0 microcoulombs; find net electric flux in N m squared per C.
questions.explanation: Gauss's law gives flux equals Q enclosed over epsilon zero. Three microcoulombs over 8.85e-12 gives about 3.39e5. Using 4 pi epsilon zero in denominator confuses this with Coulomb's law.
questions.hint: Flux equals Q over epsilon zero.

questions.explanation: Field lines from an external charge enter and leave the surface equally, so net flux is zero. They do not cancel the enclosed charge's flux; that charge's contribution remains.
questions.hint: External field lines enter and exit equally.

questions.topic: Why magnetic field lines never begin or end

answer.exemplar: Magnetic field lines form closed loops because no magnetic monopoles exist; every north pole is paired with a south pole, so lines continue through the magnet.

questions.explanation: Without magnetic monopoles, field lines cannot start or stop; they close on themselves. Electric lines begin and end on charges, but magnetic ones do not.

questions.explanation: Flux is 0.2 times 0.5 times cos60 equals 0.05 webers. Using sin gives 0.0866, wrong.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Why magnetic field lines never begin or end
questions.stem: Interpreting a graph, because magnetic lines never begin or end, the net flux through any closed surface is?

options.text: Equal to 4 pi times enclosed charge.

questions.explanation: Closed lines imply equal entry and exit, so net flux is zero. Enclosed current affects circulation, not flux.
questions.hint: Closed lines give zero net flux.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Choosing a surface that makes the flux integral easy
questions.stem: Interpreting a graph, why must a Gaussian surface be closed?

answer.exemplar: A closed surface is required so that every field line either enters and exits or stays inside, allowing Gauss's law to relate net flux to enclosed charge.

questions.explanation: Gauss's law applies to closed surfaces. An open surface has no well-defined inside, so net enclosed charge is undefined.

questions.topic: Field of a uniformly charged infinite sheet
questions.stem: Interpreting a graph, an infinite sheet has sigma 1.0 microcoulomb per square meter; find E in N/C times 1e5.
questions.explanation: E equals sigma over 2 epsilon zero equals 1e-6 over 1.77e-11 about 5.65e4, or 0.565 in units of 1e5. Using sigma over epsilon zero doubles it.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Net flux from a charge inside a closed surface
questions.stem: Interpreting a graph, enclosed charge is 10 microcoulombs; find flux in N m squared per C times 1e5.
questions.explanation: Flux is 10e-6 over 8.85e-12 about 1.13e6, or 11.3e5. Using 4 pi epsilon zero gives smaller value.
questions.hint: Flux equals Q over epsilon zero.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Why a charge outside a surface adds no net flux
questions.stem: Interpreting a graph, no charge is enclosed but an external 10 microcoulomb is nearby; find net flux in N m squared per C.
questions.explanation: No enclosed charge means zero net flux. The external charge does not contribute net flux.
questions.hint: Zero enclosed charge means zero flux.
